name: SwiftLint (SwiftSyntax-based rules)
baseline: Earlier SwiftLint releases with SourceKit-based rules (0.48 and earlier)
verdict_reason: Release notes report rule rewrites on SwiftSyntax about 7-10x faster and whole-lint gains of 6-30% per release, plus 10-15% (up to 3-4x at high concurrency) from less cache-lock contention in 0.64.0. The claims are modest and specific; they are per-release, first-party and not cumulative measurements.
tier_reason: First-party changelog entries with no benchmark project, hardware or method.
claimed_speedup: comma rule about 10x, colon about 7x, closure_spacing about 9x faster (0.49.0); lint times up to 15% faster (0.50.0); up to 6% (0.51.0); up to 30% faster (0.56.0); 10-15%, up to 3-4x at high concurrency (0.64.0)
workload: Linting Swift projects; individual rule rewrites and whole-run lint times
install: Homebrew, Mint, Swift Package Manager plugin, CocoaPods, Bazel
one_liner: The standard Swift linter; rewriting rules on SwiftSyntax made them 7-10x faster and whole runs 6-30% faster per release.
how_it_is_fast: Rules moved from SourceKit requests, which go through the compiler's service process, to SwiftSyntax tree visitors running in-process. Later releases picked up SwiftSyntax's own parser speedups and reduced lock contention on the results cache when linting with many threads.
use_it_when: Projects on SwiftLint 0.48 or earlier: upgrading is the speedup
Large codebases linted with many threads, where 0.64.0's cache-locking change helps most
skip_it_when: Analyzer rules, which still need a compiler log and are slower; the changelog reported about 2x regressions for them with Swift 5.6
caveats: Per-rule 7-10x figures do not translate into whole-lint speedups of that size
No benchmark project or hardware is named in any entry
Gains are relative to older SwiftLint, not to a different linter
tradeoffs: Newer releases require newer Swift toolchains to build

evidence.quote: Make `comma` rule about 10x faster, finding some previously missed cases and fixing some previously wrong corrections.
Make `colon` rule about 7x faster, finding some previously missed cases.

Improve linting performance by 10-15%, especially when running with many threads, by optimizing cache locking and reducing contention. Depending on the project and level of concurrency, the performance improvement can be even higher (3-4x).
Note that we've measured performance regressions compared to Swift 5.5 on the order of about 2x.
